title.en: The Spine: A Tower That Bends

text.zh: 从背后看，脊柱不是一根直棍，而是一条侧看呈两道弯的曲线。这两道弯是它能扛住你的关键。
text.en: Seen from behind, the spine is no straight rod. From the side it draws two opposing curves — and those curves are why it can carry you.

text.zh: 最上面 7 块是颈椎，最轻也最灵活。你此刻点头、摇头、转头，动的都是它们。
text.en: The top seven are the cervical vertebrae — the lightest and most mobile. Every nod, shake and turn of your head happens here.

text.zh: 往下 12 块胸椎，每一块都被一对肋骨拴住。稳固是代价，它是整条脊柱里最不能扭的一段。
text.en: Next come twelve thoracic vertebrae, each tethered to a pair of ribs. Stability has a price: this is the least twistable stretch of the whole spine.

text.zh: 再往下只剩 5 块腰椎，却要接住上半身的全部重量，所以它们长得又厚又宽。
text.en: Only five lumbar vertebrae remain below, yet they must catch the entire weight of the upper body — which is why they are built so thick and broad.

text.zh: 重量最后交给骶骨，这块三角形的骨头嵌在两侧髋骨之间，把力分给骨盆和双腿。
text.en: The load finally passes to the sacrum, a wedge of bone locked between the hip bones that splits the force out to the pelvis and both legs.

text.zh: 每两块椎骨之间都垫着一片椎间盘。它们加起来约占脊柱长度的四分之一，弯腰的角度全靠它们让出来。
text.en: Between every two vertebrae sits a disc. Together they make up roughly a quarter of the spine's length, and every degree of bending is borrowed from them.

text.zh: 这座塔是空心的。椎孔连成一条管道，脊髓就住在里面——脊柱的形状，本来就是为了护住它。
text.en: The tower is hollow. The vertebral openings line up into a canal, and the spinal cord lives inside it — the spine is shaped the way it is to guard this.

text.zh: 光靠骨头它立不住。两侧的竖脊肌像帆船上的缆绳，一直在收着——久站腰酸，就是它们喊累。
text.en: Bone alone cannot hold it upright. The erector spinae run down both sides like a sailboat's rigging, always pulling — and stand too long, and they will complain.

text.zh: 骨头、软垫、缆绳，三样东西合起来才是脊柱：既撑得住体重，又弯得下腰。
text.en: Bone, cushion and rigging — only all three together make a spine: strong enough to hold your weight, supple enough to let you bend.
